recipes.name: Mama Palomba's Spaghetti Sauce
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound hot Italian sausage, sliced into bite-sized pieces
0.5 pound mild Italian sausage, sliced into bite-sized pieces
1 tablespoon dried basil, or to taste
1 tablespoon dried oregano, or to taste
1 tablespoon dried parsley, or to taste

steps.text: Heat tomato puree in a large pot over medium-low heat; simmer while prepared the remaining ingredients.

Heat a skillet over medium heat; cook and stir hot Italian sausage, mild Italian sausage, and ground chuck until browned and cooked through, 10 to 15 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove cooked sausage and chuck with a slotted spoon and transfer to the simmering tomato puree.
Cook and stir onion and garlic in the same skillet used for browning meat until onions are lightly browned, 5 to 8 minutes. Transfer onion mixture to meat mixture.

Stir water and tomato paste in the same skillet used for onion mixture over low heat until slightly thickened, about 15 minutes; add to the sauce in the pot. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese, basil, oregano, and parsley over the sauce; stir to combine. Simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, for 3 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Mama Palomba's Spaghetti Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This Italian-inspired tomato sauce is filled with Italian sausage, ground chuck, and the right amount of herbs and spices. It is simmered on the stove for hours, for a flavorful and rich topping for your pasta.

review.reviewBody: Very easy to put together from start to finish. I will say I foobarb'ed with the Italian Sausage links, I used Hot Turkey Polish Sausage instead. Even though it worked out well. I'll have to try to use the italian sausage links the next time. Ours had a bit of a bite to it was, just a little acidic not much just a tad. However, my littliest one said she like "stagetti night" and was prouf of it ;-) Thank you LindaT.

Super yummy...I used a full pound of extra lean hot Italian chicken sausage out of the casing, cooked and crumbled, omitted the ground beef since I had none. Used four cans of crushed tomatoes with basil, added a diced red pepper and baby bella mushrooms which I cooked along with the onion and sausage. I added everything to the crockpot and it was a wonderful easy and very flavorful, chunky sauce. Served over whole wheat spaghetti and served with a salad. Family enjoyed, thanks!

Delicious! I scaled this down to 8 servings and used all fresh herbs (3x the dried amount). We had this over spaghetti tonight, and will have the remaining sauce later in the week, maybe over polenta. Thanks for the recipe Linda!

Absolutely amazing! I made this in November of 22 when I first came upon this recipe..I did not have any mild sausage in the house so I used all hot and followed the directions exactly otherwise. I love my sauce with a bite to it anyway. When it was done after simmering for the 3 hours I tasted it and couldn't taste any heat at all.i was shocked..so do not worry about it being spicy it is just for flavor and this is a delicious sauce recepe close to a bolognese. I gave away alot of it to family because I live alone and everyone loved it! People raved about this sauce. This is one of the easiest recipes I have ever made as well. I am about to make it again..this time I will keep more for me! I did add some crushed red pepper for heat and spice at the end..use your own judgement for your own tastes.

Very good did add 3 T of sun dried tomatoes and substitued red wine for water. Used a 1 pnd of ground beef instead of 2. Added some red pepper flakes to spice it up. Nice thick sauce with great flavor.

I love this recipe! The first time I made it, I made it as written, but I cut it in half. There was still MORE than enough (I was able to freeze 3 containers of it after dinner was done). I was not a fan of the hot sausage in it, to me it gave it a burnt taste. I made it again tonight, except I substituted ground turkey for the beef and used all mild sausage (my store didnt have any turkey sausage or I would have used that). I also put the meat in the food processor so there werent any huge chunks in there. After making a batch of stuffed shells for my daughter and I, I still had enough to fill 4 dishes to freeze. This sauce is better than anything I have ever bought in the store, and costs way less in the end. And it is versatile, which makes it even better!
Delicious! I add about 15 oz. Of cabernet

We just got back from Italy and I had a craving for the Spaghetti Bolognese we had there. This recipe is a keeper! Very easy to make and so scrumptious! It has the rich flavor that I loved in Italy. Everyone is the family loved it! Will definitely be making it again. 

Only change I made was instead of using 2 different sausages (hot and mild) , I just used Italian sausage to keep it easier as I didn't want to buy 2 different flavors and only use half of each.

This sauce I have placed under my “don’t knock it till you tried it “ category of recipes. I play around with the ingredients by adding whatever spices my body wants each time I use this recipe. I love garlic and onions 🧅 (fresh ingredients only), with lots of rosemary, Italian seasoning, topping it all off with a dash of sugar that doesn’t add any unnecessary sweetness, at all. The sugar just simply removes the acidity from the sauce. My husband and the rest of my family members look forward to my spaghetti sauce(s). My advice is that you don’t second guess yourself and limit your creativity in the kitchen…Go wild and have fun with it…your family will love you more for it 😇😄😎
Delicious! I halved the recipe and I used fresh herbs rather than dried. I used hot Italian sausage (never buy mild sausage) and the ground chuck. Very easy to make.
Absolutely loved this hearty and delicious meat sauce. I used fresh herbs instead of dried, tripling the amount called for. I will definitely be making this one again.
I love this stuff!!! Can eat it by the spoonful!!! I have a picky eater so I make this with tomato sauce instead of puree and onion powder instead of chopped onions. It still tastes so good!!
I am laughing at Robin May's three-star review. She did not include the sausage in her sauce! I made the sauce with called-for meats and it was delicious : )
A very rich and delicious sauce. I would consider draining the ground beef and sausage drippings, however, if you are concerned or sensitive to an abundant amount of fat in your diet.
Delicious. Subbed in Spicy Turkey Sausage and Ground Sirloin to reduce fat content. Fam loved it!

Oh, my, yum! This recipe definitely shows why slow food is better. There is a richness and depth of flavor present that cannot be duplicated by a jar sauce. Not a convenience food, but definitely worth repeating , I'm grateful Mama Palomba shared her recipe with the submitter, and I'm glad Linda shared with Allrecipes!

A perfect blend of flavors but more importantly, this sauce has a perfect consistency for using with short-cut pasta or in lasagne. It's so rich and thick, you can eat it with a fork or a piece of bread! The ratio of tomatoes to meat is right on. Thank you for the recipe.

Delicious! I made a 1/2 batch to sample before I did a double batch for a family gathering. It passed with flying colors and I ate the 1/2 batch like soup while the double batch was cooking. It is THAT good! Who needs pasta with a sauce this good? ;) Love the combination of sausage and ground beef. For the sausage I used all mild in place of hot because here in Michigan people are heat wimps. Thanks for a keeper Linda!

The best spaghetti sauce recipe I have found. So odd that 3000 people have added it to Favorites, but only a very small number have reviewed. The only change is that I used one pound of hot sausage, because I didn't want to buy a pound of hot and a pound of mild and freeze what was left. This is a fantastic sauce, and I will make it again and again.

Thick and meaty, very flexible recipe and great to freeze for last minute needs. What's not to like. I have made this with the puree, without it and using stewed tomato's, beef, chicken, turkey always good and always easy to put together. Thank you for sharing this.
